candidate_sources.title: Potato Diseases: Rhizoctonia Stem Canker and Black Scurf - MSU Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Rhizoctonia disease of potato is caused by the fungus Rhizoctonia solani Kuhn. The fungus attacks underground sprouts before they emerge from the soil (damping-off); stem lesions mature into rough, brown cankers; black to brown hard sclerotia (black scurf) form on tuber surfaces. High soil moisture, cool temperatures and neutral to acid soil favor disease development.

candidate_sources.title: Rhizoctonia Canker and Black Scurf of Potato | Cornell Vegetables
candidate_sources.snippet: Above-ground symptoms early in the season include necrosis at the tips of sprouts (damping-off, which may cause the emerging plant to die) and sunken lesions on stolons, roots, and stems. Dark brown to black sclerotia form on tuber surfaces. Black scurf and stem canker are more severe in cool, moist soils (16-23 C). Management includes certified seed, crop rotation, shallow planting in warm soil, and seed/in-furrow fungicide treatments.

candidate_sources.title: Bulletin #2273, Potato Facts: Rhizoctonia Diseases on Potatoes - University of Maine Cooperative Extension
candidate_sources.snippet: Rhizoctonia diseases on potatoes, caused by Rhizoctonia solani, include damping-off of sprouts, stem and stolon canker, and black scurf (sclerotia on tubers). Describes symptoms, disease cycle, environmental conditions favoring the disease, and integrated management practices.

candidate_sources.snippet: Potato Rhizoctonia stem canker and black scurf caused by Rhizoctonia solani AG-3. Covers damping-off of sprouts, stem cankers, aerial tubers, sclerotia formation on tubers, disease cycle, and management.
